Team — summary and immediate actions (TL;DR below). Forwarding customer samples and initial infra findings.

Initial triage notes from infra on-call:
- Symptoms: abrupt increase in 429s (request-level throttles) and elevated p95/p99 latency from inference gateway.
- Apparent trigger: our circuit-breaker / safety valve that enforces burst credits at the per-tenant level is moving to a hard-close state when the concurrent token cache eviction rate spikes. That hard-close produces immediate 429s even when the token-bucket quota still appears to have headroom.
- Why this matters: some of our recent changes to KV cache eviction and the burst-credit replenishment window reduced the effective burst buffer for a subset of tenant shapes (long-short bursty customers like Acme). The config change was rolled as part of a runtime perf tweak this week.

Proposed immediate mitigations (exec + infra approval required):
1) Temporarily increase Acme's burst allowance by lifting the per-tenant "safety-valve" threshold to 3x for 2 hours (fastest mitigation).
2) Add a routing rule to send Acme traffic to the older Dedicated pool that still has the prior burst semantics.
3) Disable the new eviction-triggered hard-close path for the circuit-breaker (flip a flag) so the safety valve becomes graceful rather than hard-close.
4) Open INF-3291 and capture logs + timeline; request a post-incident runbook update.

Attachments: infra_runbook_circuit-breaker.pdf, circuit_breaker_config.diff (the config diff that deployed Wednesday). Also attaching the customer's error samples.

Impact assessment so far: ~7% failed checkouts, estimated MRR risk if not resolved within 4 hours. Legal / account team asking for executive visibility.

TL;DR: We likely shipped a config/semantics change this week that unintentionally tightened the per-tenant burst safety valve. Recommend temporary burst increase + route to dedicated pool while we patch and run a postmortem.

—Monica
